questions.prompt: Put the checks on agent-written pipeline code in order, cheapest first.
items: Run on a tiny real input
Compare with an independent check on that input

why.Run on real data: Real data and cluster time are the expensive step, so it comes after every cheap check.

questions.prompt: Your dry run lists every expected job and exits cleanly. What have you shown?
questions.explain: A dry run shows the plan. It does not run the commands.

options.text: The workflow manager could build a plan of which steps would run
Every tool command in the pipeline runs with valid flags and arguments
options.misconception: No command was executed, so a wrong flag still passes a dry run.

options.text: The outputs will be correct once you run it on the real data
options.misconception: Nothing was computed, so nothing about the results has been tested.

options.text: The pipeline will finish within the cluster time you plan to request
options.misconception: A plan lists jobs but says nothing about how long they take.

questions.prompt: Which problems can a dry run or stub run catch, and which not?
questions.explain: These runs exercise the graph; checking the commands takes a real run.

items.text: A step needs an input that no step produces
items.misconception: Typically reported when the plan is built, though which errors appear is not guaranteed.

items.text: A tool flag that silently changes the result
items.misconception: The command never runs, so its behaviour is untested.

items.text: A process declares an output that its stub never creates
items.misconception: A stub run can expose a declared output that is not produced. A wrong but compatible connection can still pass, so read the plan too.

items.text: Filtering that drops half the reads for the wrong reason
items.misconception: That needs a real run on a tiny input and a check on the result.

questions.prompt: An agent says the new pipeline 'was tested'. Which follow-up is the most useful?
questions.explain: Ask what was run, on what input, and compared with what. Then repeat the cheap parts yourself.

options.text: Ask what was run, on which input, and what the output was compared with
Ask it to run the test suite it wrote and report whether everything passes
options.misconception: Tests the agent wrote may only check what it already believes, and its report is still its own claim.

options.text: Ask a second agent to review the pipeline and say if it looks correct
options.misconception: A second opinion from a similar system is another claim, not an observation of a run.

options.text: Look for a test file in the diff and treat it as proof of testing
options.misconception: A test file existing does not show it was run, or that it checks anything meaningful.
